title: Zero-Copy WASM Core Engine with Tier-1 JIT Compiler and Spec Conformance
objective: Implement a standalone WebAssembly (WASM MVP) core engine in C++20 featuring a streaming zero-copy binary parser/validator and a Tier-1 baseline JIT compiler generating native x86-64 machine code directly into executable memory pages (mmap with PROT_EXEC). The runtime must execute WASM control flow (block, loop, if/else, br, br_if, br_table), value stack manipulations, linear memory bounds checking, host imports/exports conforming to System V AMD64 ABI, and pass 100% of the WebAssembly Core Specification tests.
motivation: WASM is the universal runtime for serverless edge computing, plugin sandboxes, and browser execution. Building a lightweight JIT runtime tests low-level ABI calling conventions, machine code generation, register allocation, and bytecode validation.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Single-Pass x86-64 Machine Code Emission: Lowering structured WASM control blocks into native relative branch offsets while managing value stack depths and target label unwinds.
2. Linear Memory Bounds & Signal Handling: Enforcing memory safety for i32/i64 loads/stores without excessive runtime overhead via guard pages or inline limit checks.
3. Host Import/Export ABI Calling Conventions: Bridging WASM stack parameters to native System V AMD64 hardware registers (rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9) and floating-point registers (xmm0-xmm7) with zero intermediate copying.
environmentSummary: Debian 12 container with gcc-13, g++-13, clang-18, cmake 3.28, ninja-build, wabt (WebAssembly Binary Toolkit), and the W3C WASM Core Spec test suite pre-installed in /app. Starter repository provides binary section parser skeletons, x86-64 opcode buffer encoders, and unit test suites.
oracleStrategy: Reference C++20 implementation under solution/ provides a streaming LEB128 decoder, an x86-64 single-pass opcode emitter with register caching, and an mmap-backed executable memory manager conforming to W3C Core Spec.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh which executes four verification channels:
1. WASM Binary Section Parsing & LEB128 Validation (decoding Type, Import, Function, Memory, Global, Export, Code sections).
2. W3C Core Spec Control Flow & Math Conformance (testing arithmetic, loops, branches, nested blocks, and br_table).
3. Native x86-64 JIT Execution & Speedup Benchmark (verifying code executes natively via mmap PROT_EXEC and beats interpreter baseline by >5x).
4. Memory Bounds Trapping & Sanitizer Checks (testing out-of-bounds traps and ASan/UBSan clean execution).
binarySuccessCondition: Passes >= 98% of the W3C WASM core test suite, compiles to native executable x86-64 code, intercepts memory traps safely, and passes 0 sanitizer errors.
partialScoreStrategy:
Monotone scoring breakdown:
- 25%: WASM binary parsing & LEB128 decoding.
- 25%: Arithmetic & stack manipulation opcode execution.
- 25%: Structured control flow (block, loop, br_table) & function calls.
- 25%: Native x86-64 JIT compilation speedup & memory trap safety.
anticipatedExploits:
1. Linking against Wasmtime/Wasmer/V8: Verifier scans symbols, disassembles generated memory buffers, and inspects dynamic dependencies.
2. Interpreting instead of JIT compiling: Verifier verifies memory protection flags (mprotect PROT_EXEC) and enforces JIT execution throughput thresholds.
